messages:
Sam W: morning all — got a P1 latency spike in api-west-1, pages crossed at 07:04 PT. incident-bot posted details. Assigning bridge and owners.

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: P1 - inference-api 95th latency > 3s (api-west-1) — triggered 2026-03-15T07:04:12Z — link: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345 :rotating_light:

Maria L: on it. grabbing driver. quick status: user impact appears intermittent for a subset of customers on dedicated instances.

Ben C: I can be comms. I'll open the bridge and ping sales-ops. starting a bridge link and posting a customer-facing note.

Sam W: driver -> Maria L. comms -> Ben C. secondary -> Nikhil P. Sam to stay nearby for handover in ~20m.

Maria L: taking driver. first triage: checking recent deploys, metrics, and autoscale. running `kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=api --no-headers -o wide` to check pod distribution.

Maria L: Ran check — pod restarts = 0, CPU 70-90% on a few hosts, queue depth spike visible at the ingress. Looks like requests are queuing at the LB. logs: https://logs.redwood.example/r/abcdef (redacted link).

Ben C: opened bridge https://meet.google.com/xxx and posting customer note to status page. Drafting initial customer text.

Ben C: draft note: "We're investigating a latency issue affecting API calls in US-West regions. Engineers are triaging. We'll post updates every 15m." :thumbsup:

Nikhil P: APAC coverage gap this morning until 14:00 UTC — if followthrough is needed across handoff, JESS is out today; consider routing followups to infra-lead.

Sam W: Good catch. Maria — if mitigations require rolling restarts, coordinate with infra to avoid APAC disruption. Also prepare a routing fallback to `model-small` if load reduction is needed.

Maria L: Running a canary rollback to previous runtime on one node. commands:
```
# rollback candidate
kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-api -n inference --to-revision=42
```
Monitoring canary now.

incident-bot: Update: Latency improved on canary node at 07:14 PT, 95th reduced to ~1.2s. :eyes:

Ben C: updating customers. Posted update on bridge and status page; tagging #support and sales-eng.

Sam W: We're approaching my handoff in ~20m. Plan: if stable for next 10m, I'll pass primary to Nikhil with Maria as secondary (Maria remains driver until we confirm stability). If any regression, I will stay. Runbook pointer: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/api-latency.md (see section 'routing fallbacks').

Nikhil P: I can take primary at 07:30 PT. I'll update on-call notes and confirm APAC coverage options with infra.

Maria L: will keep monitoring for 15m, then hand off detailed checklist: metrics snapshot, current routing overrides, active customer list, mitigations tried, and links to logs.

Ben C: when handing off, paste the last status update and include `#customers_affected` list in the bridge chat. Also mention any throttles or routing changes.

Sam W: Agree. After handoff: Nikhil = primary (driver if no regression), Ben = comms, Maria = secondary (driver until stable). Add a note in the runbook: "handoff friction: if APAC gap exists, escalate to infra-lead@redwood.com".

Maria L: noted. :thumbsup: Will include metrics exports and the canary result in the handoff message.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline completed for inference-api at 06:50 PT (sha: abc123), no automatic rollback triggered.

Ben C: final pre-handoff update posted to bridge and status page. Mentioned expected follow-ups and that Maria will remain on driver duties for now. Passing to Nikhil at 07:30 PT.

Nikhil P: acknowledged. I'll take it from 07:30 PT, will continue watch and coordinate with infra if we need autoscaler tuning. :wave:

Sam W: handing over — thanks team. I'll stay reachable for 30m. :ok_hand:

incident-bot: Auto-summary at 07:33 PT: canary rollback reduced latency; monitoring continues; watch assigned to Nikhil P. Thread will remain open for updates.
